# LinkedIn Job Listings with Salary & Company Data Scraper

Turn LinkedIn's public job board into a clean spreadsheet. Search by keywords, locations and employers, or paste job links, and get one row per posting with the full description, a yearly salary range with its source, applicant numbers, Easy Apply status, seniority, the recruiter when LinkedIn shows one, and the employer's LinkedIn profile. No LinkedIn account, login or cookies needed.

## What this actor does

- **Salary you can sort by.** Pay is parsed into minimum, maximum, currency and period, then converted to yearly figures. It comes from LinkedIn's own pay box or, when the employer only wrote it in the description, from that text. `salarySource` tells you which.
- **Many searches in one run.** Several keywords times several locations, company-only searches, pasted LinkedIn search links and individual job links, merged without duplicates.
- **Filters that really narrow the results.** Date posted (from the past hour to the past 3 months), distance, Easy Apply, fewer than 10 applicants, companies to include or exclude, experience level, job type, industry, staffing agencies, salary and recruiter.
- **Employer profile included.** Industry, size, headquarters, website, founding year, office addresses, follower count, tagline and description, looked up once per company.
- **Empty fields are omitted.** Fields LinkedIn doesn't show for a posting are left out instead of filled with blanks or guesses.

## Output per job

| Field | What it contains |
|---|---|
| `id`, `title`, `jobUrl` | LinkedIn job ID, job title and link |
| `companyName`, `companyUrl`, `companyId`, `companyNumericId`, `companyLogo` | Employer name, LinkedIn page, page name, numeric company ID and logo |
| `location` | Location as LinkedIn shows it |
| `postedDate`, `postedDateText`, `postedAt` | Date the job was posted or last reposted, LinkedIn's "2 days ago" text, and the exact UTC posting time when LinkedIn's page shows it (Extended job page depth asks again when it's missing) |
| `expiresAt` | LinkedIn's own expiry date and time for the posting, when the job page includes structured data (present for many, but not all, postings); omitted otherwise |
| `salary`, `salaryRange`, `salarySource` | Pay as written, parsed `{min, max, currency, interval, minYearly, maxYearly}`, and `employer` (LinkedIn's pay box) or `description` |
| `applicantCount`, `applicantCountNumeric`, `applicantCountKind`, `applicantInsights` | "Over 200 applicants" as shown, the number, whether it is `exact`, `moreThan` or `fewerThan`, and early-applicant notes |
| `listingBadge`, `activelyHiring` | Badge on the search result, such as "Actively Hiring" or "Be an early applicant" |
| `easyApply`, `applyUrl` | Whether you can apply on LinkedIn, and the LinkedIn apply page |
| `descriptionText`, `descriptionHtml` | Full job description as plain text and HTML |
| `responsibilities`, `qualifications`, `preferredQualifications` | Bullet lists from the description when it has those sections |
| `seniorityLevel`, `inferredSeniorityLevel`, `employmentType`, `industries`, `industriesList` | LinkedIn's job criteria, plus a seniority taken from the title when LinkedIn says "Not Applicable" |
| `experienceYearsMin`, `experienceYearsMax` | Years of experience asked for in the description |
| `visaSponsorshipMentioned`, `visaSponsorshipPhrase` | Whether the description offers or rules out visa sponsorship, with the sentence |
| `remoteAllowed` | `true` when the title or description clearly says the job is fully remote, or when the job page's structured data marks it `TELECOMMUTE`. It is never set from hybrid or on-site guesses |
| `recruiter` | `{name, title, profileUrl, photoUrl}` of the person who posted the job, when LinkedIn shows them |
| `contactEmails` | Email addresses written in the description |
| `atsPlatform` | Hiring system (Workday, Greenhouse, Lever…) when the description links to it |
| `companyIndustry`, `companySize`, `companyHeadquarters`, `companyType`, `companyWebsite`, `companyFounded`, `companySpecialties`, `companyLocations`, `companyFollowersCount`, `companySlogan`, `companyDescription` | Employer profile from LinkedIn |
| `companyAffiliatedPages`, `companySimilarPages` | `{name, url, industry}` of the employer's subsidiaries and of similar companies, as listed on its LinkedIn page |
| `companyRecentPosts` | The employer's latest public LinkedIn posts: `{url, postedAt, text, reactionsCount, commentsCount}` |
| `similarJobs`, `peopleAlsoViewed`, `similarSearches`, `industryIds`, `titleId`, `titleCategoryLabel`, `titleCategoryUrl` | Related jobs and LinkedIn's own categories (Extended job page depth only) |
| `searchQuery`, `searchLocation`, `searchUrl` | Which of your searches found the job |
| `scrapedAt` | When the row was collected |

The dataset has three ready-made views: **Jobs**, **Salaries** (yearly minimum and maximum side by side) and **Employers**.

## Input

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `searchQueries` | array | – | Keywords to search, one per line. Each one is searched in every location |
| `searchUrls` | array | – | LinkedIn job search links copied from your browser |
| `jobUrls` | array | – | Job links or numeric job IDs to scrape directly |
| `locations` | array | – | Places in English, e.g. `Germany`, `Austin, Texas`. Empty means worldwide |
| `geoIds` | array | – | Numeric LinkedIn location IDs, for exact places |
| `distance` | string | `""` (LinkedIn default) | Radius around a city: 0, 5, 10, 25, 50 or 100 miles |
| `timePosted` | string | `""` (any time) | Past hour, 24 hours, 3 days, week, 2 weeks, month or 3 months |
| `companies` | array | – | Employer names, LinkedIn company or university page links, or company IDs |
| `excludeCompanies` | array | – | Employers to leave out |
| `easyApply` | boolean | `false` | Only Easy Apply jobs |
| `under10Applicants` | boolean | `false` | Only jobs with fewer than 10 applicants |
| `experienceLevel` | string | `""` (any) | Internship, Entry level, Associate, Mid-Senior level, Director or Executive |
| `jobType` | string | `""` (any) | Full-time, Part-time, Contract, Temporary, Volunteer, Internship or Other |
| `industry` | array | `[]` | LinkedIn industries of the employer |
| `companySizes` | array | `[]` | Only employers of these sizes (1-10 up to 10,001+ employees) |
| `excludeStaffingAgencies` | boolean | `false` | Skip staffing and recruiting firms |
| `requireSalary` | boolean | `false` | Only jobs that state their pay |
| `minYearlySalary` | integer | – | Skip jobs whose pay range tops out below this yearly amount |
| `salaryCurrency` | string | `""` (any) | Only jobs paying in this currency; also the currency of `minYearlySalary` |
| `requireRecruiter` | boolean | `false` | Only jobs that name the person who posted them |
| `includeTitleKeywords` | array | – | Title must contain one of these words |
| `excludeTitleKeywords` | array | – | Title must not contain any of these words |
| `excludeJobIds` | array | – | Job IDs from earlier runs to skip |
| `scrapeJobDetails` | boolean | `true` | Add description, salary, criteria, applicants and recruiter |
| `includeCompanyDetails` | boolean | `true` | Add the employer's LinkedIn profile |
| `enrichmentDepth` | string | `standard` | `full` adds similar jobs, related searches and LinkedIn's category IDs, and retries for the exact posting time |
| `language` | string | `en` | Language of LinkedIn's labels (English, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese) |
| `splitLargeSearches` | boolean | `true` | When a search reaches LinkedIn's 1,000-result limit, continue with narrower posting-date windows |
| `maxItems` | integer | `100` | Stop after this many jobs (up to 10,000) |

Use at least one of `searchQueries`, `searchUrls`, `jobUrls` or `companies`.

### Example: newest data jobs in three countries

```json
{
    "searchQueries": ["data engineer", "analytics engineer"],
    "locations": ["Germany", "Netherlands", "United Kingdom"],
    "timePosted": "r604800",
    "maxItems": 300
}
```

### Example: every open role at two employers, with pay only

```json
{
    "companies": ["General Motors", "https://www.linkedin.com/company/affirm"],
    "requireSalary": true,
    "maxItems": 200
}
```

### Example: check a list of postings

```json
{
    "jobUrls": [
        "https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/4419969671",
        "4336853130"
    ]
}
```

## Use cases

- **Salary benchmarking:** compare yearly pay for a title across cities, countries and employers.
- **Recruiting and sourcing:** watch fresh postings in your niche, see who is hiring and who posted each role.
- **Sales prospecting:** spot companies that are hiring fast in a segment, with their size, website and offices.
- **Job hunting:** a daily run with "Past 24 hours", Easy Apply and fewer than 10 applicants, skipping jobs you've already seen.
- **Labour-market research:** track demand, seniority mix and pay transparency over time.

## FAQ

**Do I need a LinkedIn account or cookies?**
No. The actor reads the job pages LinkedIn shows to signed-out visitors.

**Can I filter for remote, hybrid or on-site jobs?**
Neither the public search nor the job page shows the remote/hybrid/on-site label to signed-out visitors, and the search ignores the workplace filter, so a remote filter can't be offered. `remoteAllowed` is `true` when the title or description clearly says the role is fully remote, or when the job page includes LinkedIn's structured data marking it `TELECOMMUTE`. That structured block only ever marks remote jobs, never hybrid or on-site, so neither is inferred; not every remote job carries it, so the field can be missing for a remote role. Adding "remote" to your keywords narrows results to jobs that mention it. Older saved inputs that still contain the remote filter or the job-function filter keep running; those two settings are ignored and the run's status message says so.

**Why do some jobs have no salary?**
Many employers don't publish pay. The actor reads LinkedIn's pay box and pay ranges written in the description, and never estimates. `salarySource` shows where each figure came from. Expect most US jobs in pay-transparency states to have a salary, and far fewer elsewhere.

**How do I get more than 1,000 jobs?**
LinkedIn returns at most 1,000 jobs for one search. When a search reaches that limit, the actor automatically continues with the same search restricted to the past month, week, 3 days and 24 hours. Each of those returns its own results, and duplicates are removed, so one keyword and location can yield well over 1,000 jobs. For even more, add locations, keywords or companies. Turn this off with `splitLargeSearches` if you only want LinkedIn's top 1,000.

**Why can't I get the employer's own application link?**
LinkedIn only shows the external "Apply on company website" link to signed-in members. `applyUrl` is the LinkedIn page where the application starts, and `easyApply` tells you whether you can apply on LinkedIn directly.

**My location returned the wrong country.**
LinkedIn quietly searches the whole United States when it doesn't recognise a place. The actor checks every location first: an unrecognised one is matched to LinkedIn's closest suggestion or skipped with a note in the status message. Type places in English ("Germany", not "Deutschland"), or use `geoIds`.

**Which details does LinkedIn hide from signed-out visitors?**
Remote/hybrid/on-site labels, the employer's own application link, whether a job was reposted, view counts and the job-function category are only shown to signed-in members, so this actor can't return them. Expiry dates are partly available: when the job page carries structured data, `expiresAt` is LinkedIn's own expiry time. Workarounds: add "remote" to your keywords or use `includeTitleKeywords` with "remote" or "hybrid"; use `remoteAllowed` for jobs that clearly state they're fully remote or whose structured data marks them `TELECOMMUTE`; use `postedDate` (the latest posting date) for freshness; to track reposts and closures yourself, run on a schedule and compare `id` values between runs. The exact posting time (`postedAt`) appears only on some versions of a job page. Extended job page depth asks again to fill it for most jobs, but not all; `postedDate` is always filled.

**How do I get only new jobs on a schedule?**
Use "Date posted: Past 24 hours", or keep the `id` values from earlier runs and pass them in `excludeJobIds`.

**Do I need to set up a proxy?**
No. The actor picks its connection automatically and switches when LinkedIn slows it down.

**Is this affiliated with LinkedIn?**
No. It is an independent tool that reads LinkedIn's public job pages.
